summary: Configured node1 to prevent usb-storage from loading immediately and after reboot. The RHEL release and kernel were preserved, and the node fully recovered after a verified restart.
actions_performed: Created /etc/modprobe.d/usb-storage-blacklist.conf with both `blacklist usb-storage` and `install usb-storage /bin/false`.
Verified an actual module-load attempt failed and usb_storage remained absent.
Restarted node1 safely, confirmed its boot identity changed, and repeated the load-denial test.
Confirmed system health, SSH access, filesystem data, configuration checksums, and cleanup after restart.

evidence.summary: Installed the root-owned SELinux-labeled policy; an actual modprobe attempt returned failure and usb_storage remained unloaded.

evidence.requirement: Prevent usb-storage from loading after reboot
evidence.summary: After the verified reboot, usb_storage was automatically absent before testing; the persistent policy remained intact and another real load attempt failed.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remained unchanged, with the os-release checksum matching before and after.

Captured healthy baseline and boot ID 7223d5b7-fa56-4ff3-acee-959a5cf5f146, acknowledged the scheduled reboot, observed new boot ID d92863bf-e91a-44b0-a3d4-b87e390b306d, then proved system state running, no failed units, SSH active, root XFS read-write, and preserved machine identity.

evidence.requirement: Preserve existing configuration and remove temporary residue
evidence.summary: Pre-existing modprobe configuration checksums matched the baseline, only the intended usb-storage policy was added, no temporary test files remained, and no failed units were present.
